issues.description: The template defines the QFT entry point with a different method name than the solution and than what the exercise tasks imply. The template declares _qft_circuit_n_qubits(...) (leading underscore) while the solution implements qft_circuit_n_qubits(...). This name/signature mismatch is structural: tests or instructor code that expect qft_circuit_n_qubits will not find it in the template, which will confuse students and prevent them from following the provided solution pattern.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits (remove the leading underscore) so the template signature matches the solution and the exercise/test expectations. Ensure the inverse method name remains qft_circuit_n_qubits_inverse so both forward and inverse QFT entry points are consistently named.

issues.description: The template declares the QFT-for-n-qubits method with a leading underscore (_qft_circuit_n_qubits) while the solution implements the same conceptual routine without the underscore (qft_circuit_n_qubits). This inconsistent identifier for the same concept (implementing the QFT for an arbitrary number of qubits) can confuse students when they compare their template/stub to the reference solution or when following instructions for Exercise 7.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across template and solution. Rename the template method _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits (remove the leading underscore), or alternatively change the solution to define _qft_circuit_n_qubits so both artifacts share the same identifier.
